title: Declaration-only Plugin SPI and named contracts for hook and pipe slots
summary: Plugins are pure declarations (`id()` + `register()`); `boot()`, `BasePlugin`, `DependsOnPlugins`, `PluginContext::dependencies()` and `PluginDependencyMissingException` are gone; before/after hooks and change pipes have the named contracts `BeforeHook`, `AfterHook`, `ChangePipe`; closures are accepted only with a signature checked at compile time; duck typing and invocation by parameter name are removed from these slots; the `azguard/*` id prefix is reserved for plugin classes under `AzGuard\`.
why: D8: one named contract per slot, no second lifecycle route, no plugin-identity dependency (owner principle 4), no dynamic invocation (principle 6). Hard risks: a hook closure whose types do not match must fail at compilation, not at the first request; the `OnceTerminal` guard (continue exactly once, writer result cannot be forged) must stay intact (I10); a plugin still declaring `boot()` compiles and is never called.

include: `Contracts\Plugins\Plugin` exactly as knowledge/contracts#plugins (Spi(Implement), since 0.7); `Plugins\PluginContext` without `dependencies()` (Spi(Call)); retire `Plugins\BasePlugin`, `Contracts\Plugins\DependsOnPlugins`, `Exceptions\PluginDependencyMissingException` (type-map retire rows); `PanelCompiler::boot()` and `dependencies()` removed

Compilation (`PanelCompiler`): each hook/pipe entry is an instance or class-string of its contract, or a closure whose parameter count, parameter types and return type match the contract method (Reflection); otherwise `DefinitionException` naming slot, origin and mismatch; `isPipe()` duck typing removed

`BeforeStage`/`AfterStage` call `$hook->before($request, $context)` / `$hook->after($request, $context, $decision)` positionally (closures invoked positionally); `RuntimeInvoker` no longer used by these stages (it stays for policies); `OnceTerminal` calls `ChangePipe::handle()` positionally
Reserved ids (D16): `Plugin::id()` starting with `azguard/` from a class outside namespace `AzGuard\` → `PluginConflictException`

Audit plugin and every in-repo plugin/pipe/hook (core `Plugins\Audit\*`, `Testing\Contracts\{ObservedPlugin,ObservedPipe,CancellingPipe}`, stubs of `azguard:make:plugin|pipe`, tests, docs/advanced/hooks-and-plugins.md) implement the contracts; `Testing\Contracts\{PluginContractTests,HookContractTests}` cover the new rules
Migration lines: boot()/BasePlugin/DependsOnPlugins removal, hook/pipe contracts and closure signatures, reserved id prefix
exclude: Change participants (P2.11) — `RecordChange` stays a pipe until then

reads.why: Rules every P2 item follows (reference wins, no shims, D17 placement, attributes, snapshots, migration lines)
Report-mode allowlist protocol and which entries this item removes
Exact validation commands and driver environment
Plugin SPI, slot table, compilation and sealing rules
Plugin queue, dependencies(), boot(), isPipe() to change

rules: Hook/pipe failure semantics are unchanged: before exception → failed decision `hook_error`; after exception reported, decision unchanged; pipe must call `$next` once (OnceTerminal) and core final validation runs after the last pipe (PipesTest, FinalValidationTest unchanged in substance).

A test proves a plugin implementing an extra `boot()` method compiles and `boot()` is never called; another proves each closure mismatch kind (count, parameter type, return type) fails at compilation.
Exceptions snapshot (`Formats/exceptions.json`) is regenerated for the retired exception (D16).
